speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you're experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, and weight loss, along with an enlarged lymph node above your collarbone. How long have you been noticing these symptoms, and has the lymph node grown since you first saw it? Do you have any fever or recent travel history?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of drenching night sweats, significant weight loss, and an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node raises concern for a malignancy, so I need to know if you have experienced any fevers or a persistent cough. Do you have a history of smoking, or have you noticed any other lumps or swelling elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the new finding of a fixed, painless neck swelling alongside your supraclavicular node, I need to clarify if you have experienced any difficulty swallowing, hoarseness, or unexplained bleeding. Have you also noticed any skin changes like itching or a rash?

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal fullness and tightening clothes suggest possible organ enlargement or fluid accumulation, which, combined with your lymph node findings, is very concerning. Do you have any history of alcohol use, and have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes? I will now order some tests to evaluate your blood and abdominal organs. speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98°F), Blood Pressure 135/80 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min.
